findings.summary: fit_temperature's hard-coded search bounds (0.5, 2.0) are too narrow for the calibration cases this module exists to handle, so minimize_scalar silently clamps to a boundary instead of returning the true MLE.
findings.mechanism: Verified numerically: for a well-calibrated synthetic set the unconstrained NLL minimum is T≈0.10, but bounds=(0.5, 2.0) forces the bounded optimizer to return T≈0.500 (pinned at the lower edge). For the overconfident synthetic set the unconstrained minimum is T≈15.8, but the same bounds force T≈2.000 (pinned at the upper edge). In both cases the returned 'fitted' temperature is just the boundary value, not a genuine optimum, and calibrate_and_persist writes this clamped value to disk with no indication it hit a bound — for realistically overconfident models (a common case this module is meant to correct) the persisted temperature will be silently capped at 2.0 regardless of how miscalibrated the model actually is.
